metadata.title: Atomic batch ingestion
metadata.text:
Atomic batch ingestion

# Atomic batch ingestion

The upsert_batch API validates every vector before mutation, allocates IDs in input order and commits all rows in one LMDB transaction. One vector-file synchronization and checkpoint serve the entire batch. An empty batch changes nothing. LMDB map capacity failure rolls back all rows and ID allocation.

metadata.title: Metadata filtering
metadata.text:
Metadata filtering

# Metadata filtering

A metadata filter checks whether a string belongs to a stored array, such as a project tag. Filtered nearest-neighbor queries use exact search to preserve completeness for selective filters. The application can attach tags, source file paths, document titles and chunk positions to each embedded paragraph.

metadata.title: Incremental HNSW
metadata.text:
Incremental HNSW

# Incremental HNSW

An existing graph snapshot can seed incremental insertion after clean mutations and reopening. Only new nodes undergo construction; previous neighbors and deleted routing links are retained. Deleted IDs are excluded from results. Refresh still hydrates vectors and rewrites a full snapshot. Compaction removes deleted graph nodes and reclaims vector space.

metadata.title: Collection identity
metadata.text:
Collection identity

# Collection identity

Database-wide monotonic vector IDs prevent cross-collection collisions. A collection handle is bound to its generation. Deleting and recreating a collection creates a new generation, so old handles are rejected as stale. Deletion checks ownership and refuses to remove a foreign collection vector.

metadata.title: Supported platforms and concurrency
metadata.text:
Supported platforms and concurrency

# Supported platforms and concurrency

The alpha supports Linux and macOS on local little-endian filesystems. A directory lock excludes other processes. Cloned handles share an operation mutex that serializes queries and writes into coherent snapshots. External file mutation and network filesystems are unsupported; parallel reads are not yet implemented.

metadata.title: Crash recovery
metadata.text:
Crash recovery

# Crash recovery

LMDB is the durable authority. Every insert transaction commits vector payloads, metadata, locations, IDs and a pending recovery marker. If a process dies before the vector file is synchronized, reopening rebuilds the file from committed payloads and checkpoints the marker. A post-commit I/O error may mean success; blindly retrying can duplicate documents.

metadata.title: Release automation
metadata.text:
Release automation

# Release automation

GitHub Actions verifies formatting, Clippy, default and optional features, Linux and macOS tests, Rust 1.88 compatibility and packaging. Dependency security audits and license checks run separately. Version tags produce a draft GitHub release with the verified crate, a checksum manifest and an OIDC-backed signature. Crates.io publication is not automatic.

metadata.title: Vector file layout
metadata.text:
Vector file layout

# Vector file layout

A vector file has VDB2 magic and a 32-byte header containing dimension, appended-block count and a checksum. Each block stores little-endian float32 values, a payload checksum and padding to a 32-byte boundary. Mmap readers validate block alignment, length and checksums before exposing zero-copy slices.
